title: Hauling is the thing you outgrow: the free tier is six people and forty tiles, the belts carry 62% by day one's end, and the belts that 'went nowhere' never did

verified.THE HEADLINE, on the reference run, meas: artifacts/H2_oldbal_newruler is first_night 24000 ticks with the SHIPPED balance rules and the new honest counters, so old and new are read with one ruler. OLD: hauled 19578, items_moved_total 2592 -> belts carry 11.7% of item movements; fuel arrivals 1040 by arm against 1036 by porter (50.1%). NEW (artifacts/H2_ref2): hauled 1961, items_moved_total 3180 -> belts 61.9%; fuel arrivals 1245 by arm against 797 by porter (61.0%). Haul capacity 76.0 items/s at range 96 -> 6.0 items/s at range 40.
verified.BELTS BY DAY THREE \u2014 they are ahead: belt share of item movements, NEW vs OLD: t1000 0%/0% (no belt exists yet), t2000 34%/28%, t2500 51%/35%, t4000 65%/14%, t8000 67%/9%, t16000 68%/11%, t24000 62%/12%. The first belt tile is laid at t1870 by the scenario; belts pass hauling 610 ticks later and stay ahead for the remaining 21500. Under the old rules belts peak at 35% and then COLLAPSE as the porter crew grows with the population.
verified.HAULING IS STILL THE ANSWER ON DAY ONE \: (1) first_night day 1: at t1000, before any belt exists, 100% of goods move by hand in both builds, and every survival series is unchanged against the parent balance — deaths 2, hope 30.16 vs 30.17, population 59, final avg_warmth 58.35, minimum avg_warmth 58.35, minimum heat.total_supply 30.0, frozen_buildings 1, all identical. Worst instantaneous heat.total_supply divergence over the whole run is -6.7 of 111 at t2340; worst citizens.avg_warmth divergence is 0.01. (2) careless_night, the scenario built for a player who plays badly: items_moved_total is 0 in BOTH runs (this player lays no belt at all) and the run ends identical — deaths 2, hope 32.26, population 34, avg_warmth 65.46, min warmth 45.47, frozen 2. Hauling got 12% dearer (494 -> 436) and nothing else moved.
verified.THE 91% \u2014 what the porters were act: 17908 of 19578 hauled items in the reference run were TWO STORES THAT BOTH REQUESTED COAL taking it off each other. The flow diagnostic names them: store 96 (the coal yard) -> store 179: 8555, and 179 -> 96: 9353. Store 179 is the crate the scenario places at (132,132) at t1850 with a standing 350-coal request. That is 4.7x more coal than the whole map contains, moved forever, and it is why 'the belts carry 12%' was true. LogiStore.spare() is the one-line rule: a store is a source only for what it holds ABOVE its own request.
verified.THE FOURTH HOLE, which the first pass of: Every STORE was priced by distance and refused past HAUL_RANGE, and then the construction stockpile branch handed the city's whole yard out at doorstep price to any cell on the map, because 'the stockpile is the city's own yard: near by definition'. That branch was 1211 of 1980 hauled items — 61% — so the range cap and the cost curve were true of 39% of hauling and a comment about the rest. LogiHaul.yard is now the Hearth's cell, read on a 400-tick timer from [P11] and named in the log ('the city's yard is the Hearth at (126,126)'), and stockpile deliveries pay the same curve and hit the same cap. Effect on the reference run: hauled 1980 -> 1961, belts 61.3% -> 61.9%, fuel by arm 60.0% -> 61.0%, burner-short samples 364 -> 407 of 1200, deaths/hope/population/warmth/frozen unchanged. by_reach also stopped lying: the doorstep bucket fell from 1211 to 109 because stockpile carries now record the distance they were actually walked.
verified.THE THREE ABLATIONS \u2014 run in three: 1. BALANCE reverted (spare() back to count(), PORTER_RATE 4.0, HAUL_RANGE 96, cost 1+d/96, _crew() back to BASE_PORTERS + population/4): tests/logistics/test_logistics_haul.gd goes 8 tests / 15 assertions RED. 2. INSTRUMENTS reverted (fuel_by_machine back to int(world.delivered_as_fuel), arms_with_no_target() and lines_to_nowhere() back to returning nothing): 4 more tests RED. 3. YARD reverted (stockpile branch back to cost 1.0, no cap): 2 more RED. Three tests stay green under all three on purpose — they are the don't-overcorrect guards (a real surplus must still move, a full belt with an arm on it is not a dead end, the Hearth's doorstep is still the cheapest delivery in the game).
verified.WHY THREE LINES WERE 'BLOCKED FOR 80% OF: Lines 1-3 are ONE chain: belt (117,121)->(125,121) hands to an underground pair (126..129,121) which hands to belt (130,121)->(137,121), loaded by one inserter at (116,121) out of the coal yard and unloaded by four arms at (119/123/131/135, 122) into the burner row. `blocked` counts ticks the front item could not hand off, so on a line whose last tile is bare ground it is a synonym for FULL. The loader was idle only 4828 of 24000 ticks; two of the four unloading arms were idle 21104 and 19357. Supply beat demand. The balance change is visible in exactly this number: line 1 and line 2 went from 79.8% and 81.4% blocked to 30.0% and 30.0%, because the porters no longer beat the belt to the burners. Line 3 stays at 80.2% and always will — it is the terminating unloading line and its last tile has nowhere to hand off by construction.
verified.WHY TWO LINES END IN sink_id -1 \u2014 b: Line 3 ends at (137,121) with arms at (131,122) and (135,122) taking off its flank; line 4 ends at (127,132) with four arms at (127..130,131) above it. A belt that terminates behind its last unloading arm has no sink by definition. Line 4's 'items 0, saturation 0, blocked 0' is not a dead line either: arm 188 at (130,131) sits on the belt's FIRST tile and clears it instantly (rate 1.39/s, idle 0), while arms 185-187 are idle 22064+ ticks because there is never anything left for them — a layout a player might legitimately want, and one nothing in this build could distinguish from a mistake.
verified.SO THE BUILD NOW ANSWERS THE QUESTION IT: Swept every 20 ticks, published as logistics.arms_no_target and logistics.lines_to_nowhere in state.json and metrics.csv, and SPOKEN once each in the log with the cell after a 400-tick grace period, then re-raised to the [P17] panel every 160 ticks (under its 12-second bus TTL, or a standing fault silently leaves the screen). Deliberately NOT 'idle' (three of four arms on the Hearth's face are idle all day and correct), NOT 'empty target' (every arm points at empty ground while its burner is still a construction site), NOT 'target full', and NOT 'backed up'.
verified.THE FRAME. artifacts/H2_nowhere_ship/sho: xvfb-run tools/run_visual.sh --scenario=res://tests/logistics/belt_to_nowhere.json — no private scene, nothing staged or suppressed, the same UI the game ships. The ATTENTION panel at t700 carries BOTH rows, and I read the PNG: '! An arm is reaching into empty ground - ... x2' and '! This belt ends in open ground and nothing takes...'. The other half of the claim is in the same run's shots/still_building.world.png at t200: lines_to_nowhere and arms_no_target are ALREADY 1 in metrics.csv and the panel is not drawn at all, because a belt is a belt to nowhere for the second between the first tile and the second and an assistant that shouts mid-drag is worse than none.
verified.AND THE SHIPPED REFERENCE RUN SAYS NOTHI: The ordinary xvfb-run tools/run_visual.sh --scenario=first_night (artifacts/H2_shipped_vis, 11 shots) reaches lines_to_nowhere 1 for exactly 6 of 1200 samples — t280-t360 and t1940, while the drag is happening — never crosses the 400-tick grace, and there is not one dead-end line in log.txt or one dead-end row in any of the eleven ATTENTION panels. Its state.json carries the balance numbers too (hauled 1980, items_moved_total 3142, porters 6, haul_capacity 6.0): the visual run and the headless run agree exactly.
verified.THE RULER THAT WAS LYING \u2014 logistic: It published world.delivered_as_fuel, which counts fuel that reached a bunker BY ANY ROUTE including a porter's back. tests/gate/expectations.json and progress/parts/E4.json both read the band as '1040 by machine against 1029 by porter - the machines now carry more of this city's fuel than the people do'. 1029 of that 1040 WERE the porters; the arms had carried eleven units. fuel_by_machine is now world.fuel_by_arm (arms only), the any-route total is still published as fuel_delivered, and the claim the band makes is now TRUE on its own terms: 1245 by arm against 797 by porter.
verified.RESEARCH \u2014 logistics.throughput_mul: Two research nodes (Hand Carts, Logistic Scheduling) wrote logistics.throughput_mult and nothing in the build read it, so Hand Carts promised +10% hauling and delivered a number nobody looked at. LogisticsSystem._read_tech reads it on a 200-tick timer into haul.rate_mult and it multiplies the crew that ALREADY exists, per ARCHITECTURE.md 7. It is now the only thing that makes a porter faster, which is what makes it worth taking.

verified.THREE WAYS TO COUNT IT, ALL OF THEM, SO: (1) THE CRITIC'S OWN PAIR, logistics.items_moved_total vs hauled: 2592/19578 (11.7%) -> 3180/1961 (61.9%). items_moved_total counts a hand-off OUT of a segment, so an item crossing a three-segment chain is counted three times; it measures traffic on the network, not arrivals. (2) FUEL ARRIVALS, one count per unit, the two channels competing for the same job: 1040 by arm against 1036 by porter (50.1%) -> 1245 against 797 (61.0%). (3) THE LEAST FLATTERING: arrivals at a destination across ALL goods — arms 1040 against porters 19578 (5.0%) -> arms 1245 against porters 1961 (38.8%). Porters still deliver more raw arrivals than arms do, because a large share of hauling is small requester top-ups that no belt in this layout serves. Every one of the three moves the same way and by a similar factor; (2) is the one I would defend as the headline because it is the only one where both channels are doing the identical job.

Of first_night's 6 contract FAILs exactly one is logistics — lines_dry, see `open` — and of endurance's 2, neither is ('every wave ends' and 'shots / enemy', both [P07]/[P08]).

open: tests/gate/expectations.json first_night `logistics.lines_dry: {max: 0}` — 'every one of 1200 samples must be zero'. IT WAS ALREADY RED ON THE PARENT, and I measured that rather than assuming it: tools/assert_run.py reports `FAIL logistics.lines_dry max 0  high 1` on artifacts/H2_base (parent code) and on my controlled old-balance ablation artifacts/H2_oldbal_newruler, where the episode is t1280-t2120. On my build it is high 2 and the episode is t1280-t3100 plus one 20-tick blip at t14760 — 94 samples of 1200 against 43. Nothing downstream moves: min heat.total_supply 30.0, min avg_warmth 58.35, deaths 2, frozen_buildings 1, all identical to the parent. It is the designed interlock working harder — [P03] stands the porters down for any burner an arm is feeding, and the crate BEHIND that arm is now filled by a six-person crew instead of a nineteen-person one, so the belt takes about fifty more seconds to get going on day one. I did NOT move the band and I did NOT soften the interlock: softening it is the 'porters quietly cover for a cut belt' fallback the interlock exists to forbid, and moving a threshold to turn a red green is the thing this project has been burned by twice. The honest options are the integrator's: accept a bounded startup transient and say so in the band, or have first_night stock the crate at t1850 instead of leaving the porters to fill it.

tests/gate/expectations.json's `logistics.fuel_by_machine` band still PASSES (1245 against a floor of 700) but its prose is now stale and was never true: it reads '1040 by machine against 1029 by porter — the machines now carry more of this city's fuel than the people do'. 1029 of that 1040 WERE the porters, because the metric published world.delivered_as_fuel (any route). The claim is true for the first time now — 1245 by arm against 797 by porter — but somebody who owns tests/gate/ should rewrite the sentence and the number. progress/parts/E4.json line 16 carries the same false claim and is not mine to edit either.

[P17]: in artifacts/H2_nowhere_ship/shots/named.world.png (t2200) only ONE of the two dead-end rows is on screen. Both are live and both are in the bus lane; the ATTENTION panel caps at 5 rows and by t2200 a council row and a narrative row out-rank the belt row. Both appear together in the same run's both_named.world.png at t700, which is the frame to read. Nothing to fix in logistics — flagged so the t2200 frame is not read as the detector failing.

[P05]: the six porters are FREE. Nobody is taken off another job to carry a sledge, so the cost a player feels is scarcity and distance, not headcount. Making the haul crew literal citizens — six people who are therefore not smelting — would make the cost of not automating explicit, and that is on their side of the fence. I deliberately did NOT reach into citizens: the previous coupling (`BASE_PORTERS + population/4`) is exactly the hole this change closes.

[P19]/[P20]: nothing in the interface says the porters are the bottleneck. haul_capacity (6.0 items/s), the carry-distance histogram (haul.by_reach) and stock_out_of_range are all in state.json and metrics.csv and none of them is on screen. A player who is being throttled by the haul network today learns it by watching a requester starve. A lens that paints 'this building is hand-fed and the crew is at capacity' would turn this balance change into a legible one.

PERF NOT MEASURED BY ME. Four cores shared with other agents, and two other Godot processes were running throughout. The new work per tick is one 20-tick sweep over the arms and the segments (10 arms, 4 lines in the reference run) and a 400-tick buildings_of_kind() scan for the Hearth; logistics' own step average is 273 us over the last 1000 ticks of first_night, unchanged. The integrator must re-measure on a quiet box.

deep_chain (43200 ticks) and economy_60min (72000 ticks) were NOT re-run — they are 4 and 7 minutes of a busy box each, and their logistics bands are weak (`items_moved final_min 1` on economy_60min). first_night, careless_night and steady_hand were all A/B'd. Somebody should put deep_chain through before this ships, because it is the only scenario with a real production chain on it and it is where a six-porter crew would bite hardest.
